verdict.rationale: SendGrid documents a first-party domain authentication feature (a UI guide on configuring domain authentication). Community users say it lets senders pass SPF/DKIM checks, including when sending on behalf of clients. However, the pack only shows a UI-based setup page and a one-line description, with no detail on the end-to-end flow the story asks for. Missing for 10: evidence that SendGrid generates the exact SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, DMARC coverage, documentation of the verification step, and an API endpoint exposing verification status.

support.subject: As a developer, I can authenticate my sending domain end to end — the product generates the exact SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS records, verifies them, and exposes verification status via the API

citations.quote: Domain authentication verifies the legitimacy of your email servers, messages, and sending addresses.
One thing Sendgrid is good at is letting people easily send emails on behalf of their clients while still passing SPF/DKIM checks
